paragraphs.source_en: Early in the eleventh month of Tenshō 17, messengers from Hōjō Ujinao of Odawara and from the Grand Minister Toyotomi Hideyoshi arrived one after the other at Tokugawa Ieyasu's residence in Sunpu. Ujinao's envoy was Matsuda Owari-no-kami Norihide, a senior retainer of Odawara. When Norihide came before Ieyasu, he sounded him out: “My lord says that if Your Lordship will mediate, he is willing to consider going to the capital.”

paragraphs.source_en: Hideyoshi had become a father at fifty-four—what changes would this extraordinary event bring to the realm through this great hero? Some said it would transform his understanding of human feelings and worldly affairs; others dismissed the notion. Yet he certainly seemed to have recovered the imperious vigor of youth and often rebuked his attendants. Judging by his manner, he might truly carry his wars as far as Ming China and India. The Hideyoshi of the present seemed rejuvenated, and no one could withstand his edge.
